identity.title: Judge Decoding: Faster Speculative Sampling Requires Going Beyond Model Alignment

problem.claim: LLM inference slows as model size grows, motivating faster autoregressive generation.

gap.claim: Standard speculative decoding rejects many objectively valid draft continuations because verification depends on draft–target alignment, limiting speedup.

contributions.claim: A judge-based verification strategy that trains a compact module over target-model embeddings to judge the current continuation.
TokenCourt, a dataset designed to elicit continuation-judgement capability in the target model.
An 8B/405B-Judge configuration for the Llama-3.1 family.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by adapting speculative-decoding verification to recognize correct but non-aligned replies, drawing on LLM-as-a-judge capabilities.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GPT-4o and human text do not achieve high acceptance rates under standard verification.
On Llama-3.1, the authors report a 9× speedup over Llama-405B while maintaining quality across a large range of benchmarks.
In optimized inference frameworks, they report up to 141 tokens/s for 8B/70B-Judge on 2 H100s and 129 tokens/s for 8B/405B on 8 H100s.

narrative_sequence.summary: Growing LLM size improves performance but makes inference slower.
Speculative decoding proposes tokens with a fast draft model and verifies them in parallel, but often rejects valid continuations under alignment-based verification.
The authors report low acceptance even for GPT-4o and human text, then ask whether verification can recognize correct non-aligned replies.
They use judge-style continuation scoring with TokenCourt and a compact embedding module, reporting speed and quality results on Llama-3.1.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a concrete failure mode—rejection of valid but non-aligned continuations—to a revised verification objective.

lessons.interpretation: A useful research framing can target the evaluator or acceptance rule rather than only improving the proposal generator.
lessons.application: When a pipeline rejects acceptable outputs, define and test an acceptance criterion that captures task correctness beyond exact agreement with a reference model.
lessons.exception: This is unsuitable when exact target-model sampling fidelity is the primary requirement.

source_observation.claim: The method is introduced through a compact module and a purpose-built dataset, followed by deployment-oriented throughput reports.

lessons.interpretation: A focused auxiliary component can make a verification redesign operationally measurable.
lessons.application: Pair a specialized supervision resource with explicit system-level metrics when proposing an inference-time module.
lessons.exception: Throughput metrics alone are insufficient when the main contribution is theoretical or when quality cannot be summarized by the reported benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark identities, quality metrics, acceptance rates, training details, or the exact verification rule.
The reported speedups and throughput are author-reported; conditions needed to assess comparability and trade-offs are not fully given.
